body.name: support-aware initial and regenerated token compiler
body.construction: Given the normalized retained expansion \(G_H^N\), form the initial selector agenda by listing exactly the selector-gate occurrences that are present in context-labelled kernels with labels \(s\in H\), in the topological order of \(G_H^N\) and then the lexicographic context and row order.  Every listed selector token is support licensed and syntactically eligible.  After the selector agenda is empty, apply the following recursive case splitter to the current labelled CADMG problem: first remove the nonempty set of nonancestors of \(Y\), if any; otherwise split when the current graph has more than one district; otherwise apply the canonically least reachable fixing operation, if one exists; and declare the state residual-ready exactly when none of these three cases applies.  At initialization and after every transition, retain only the dependency-topologically ordered agenda for the chosen current case; no token preceding the first eligible token is stored.  For a successful derivation produced by Algorithms 1--2 of Lee, Ghassami, and Shpitser using contexts in \(H\), compile its finite derivation DAG in dependency-topological order, breaking ties by the published stable vertex order and then context order.  The remaining agenda is regenerated as exactly the unexecuted suffix after deletion of the executed head.  The compiler introduces no transition relation other than \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{sc}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{fix}}\), \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{elim}}\), and \(\Rightarrow_{\mathrm{res}}\).
